The *Tatiyanāvāvimānavatthu* (Vv 8), translated as the "Third Ship Mansion," is a verse narrative preserved in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. In this text, a celestial being (*deva*) explains the karmic fruits and merit accumulated from a past virtuous deed, specifically recounting how she offered water to a monk who had fallen [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations listed on SuttaCentral include renderings across five languages, among them an English version by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral identify the text's primary counterparts as the two immediately preceding discourses in the collection, the *Paṭhamanāvāvimānavatthu* (Vv 6) and the *Dutiyanāvāvimānavatthu* (Vv 7), alongside a resembling parallel in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (*Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*, Ne 37) [SuttaCentral]. Automatically computed text-reuse data from DharmaNexus strongly aligns with these curated parallels, showing extensive mutual formulaic phrasing between Vv 8 (§0.1–12.4) and both Vv 6 and Vv 7 (§0.1–10.4) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus identifies widespread shared passages across the *Vimānavatthu* corpus—notably with the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), the *Tiladakkhiṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 10), and the *Pīṭhavimānavatthu* group (Vv 1–4)—as well as extensive incorporation in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* and partial overlap with the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Low-scoring cross-language alignments are also registered by DharmaNexus with Tibetan Mahāyāna sūtras (such as D0082 and D0261), representing machine-generated phrase matches rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
